## General quadratic biform ranks from two kernel indices

The [quadratic-kernel theorem](research/ai/2026-10-23-quadratic-kernel-indices/proof.md)
makes the rank of every nonzero `u(x)+z*v(x)+z^2*w(x)` slice computable
over any field, with coefficient degrees below a, a>=2 and b>=3.
After common-factor normalization, let D be the largest coefficient degree.
The two polynomial-kernel indices sum to aD; the first is the first degree
at which the explicit recurrence coefficient matrix has a nonzero kernel,
which occurs by floor(aD/2). The full source rank is
`ab+min(b,mu1)+min(b,mu2)`. For positive D, a zero first index is equivalent
to a fixed ground-field linear factor in the homogeneous z-quadratic.
This specializes the prior kernel-bundle identity and adds an effective
two-index procedure. Exact finite controls compare 2010 complete source
matrices, including the earlier equal-resultant ranks14/15 and their
characteristic-two behavior. Claim `AI-QUADRATIC-KERNEL-INDICES-001` is
written and unreviewed. No source-space cap, compatible matrix target,
singular degeneration or exponent improvement is established.

Codex work. The literal crossed source and its general kernel-bundle rank
identity retain their prior repository credit. Grothendieck splitting is
external mathematics, used in the arbitrary-field form of Schoemann and

case. Earlier affine, constant-endpoint, top-coefficient and resultant
counterexample packages retain their separate credit. Exact source-matrix
comparisons and same-session checking are not independent mathematical
review, formalization, historical priority or an exponent improvement.

The [general quadratic kernel package](ai/2026-10-23-quadratic-kernel-indices/proof.md)
determines individual slice ranks through two polynomial-kernel indices,
whose sum is aD and whose first nonzero-kernel degree is computable by a
bounded exact coefficient-matrix test. It explains the distinct indices
of the earlier equal-resultant examples and characterizes the zero first
index by a fixed ground-field linear factor. Do not repeat coefficient
degree or pairwise-resultant-only searches. Further structural work should
bound the positive first index or impose compatible three-leg maps; the
single-slice formula does not supply a matrix target. Written, unreviewed.
